extDescription.message: Presents one coherent invented machine to every site — the same one in the window, in every frame and in every worker.

popupNoHttpTab.message: Open an http or https tab to set it apart

popupStandDownWhy.message: This site restricts Trusted Types or refuses blob: workers, so its own workers read the real machine. The window answers the same way — otherwise the site sees a contradiction in two lines. Country, zone, locale and canvas noise work as usual. The “CSP → workers” switch below is the lever for a site like this.

popupAriaCsp.message: Rewrite the site’s CSP so the substitution reaches its workers

popupHintNormal.message: The device profile is substituted in full

popupHintStealth.message: Fewer patches — a lower score on the checks

popupScreenDropped.message: The screen is not substituted: $1×$2 is smaller than your $3×$4, and pages will see yours. Only a row at least as large as your screen on both sides is substituted.

popupScreenRest.message: Everything else — cores, memory, GPU — works as usual.

popupExitTitle.message: The profile claims $1 ($2) while requests leave from an address in $3 ($4). Any site can see that disagreement without a line of JS. Change the country or the VPN node.

popupSavedOpenF5.message: Saved — open a site and press F5

popupPickFirst.message: Choose a profile and a country

popupSwFailed.message: Could not switch the Service Worker

popupOpenHttpF5.message: — open an http tab and press F5

popupCspOnTitle.message: This site’s CSP is rewritten: our workers get through and the site’s nonce policy is weakened. Switch it off to restore the site’s own header.

popupCspNeededTitle.message: The site’s CSP refuses our workers, so the substitution is paused here (see the Limits). Switch it on to rewrite the header — that lowers the site’s own XSS protection.

popupCspNotNeeded.message: The site’s CSP does not block the substitution — the switch is not needed.

popupCspUnneeded.message: The site’s CSP does not block the substitution — nothing was rewritten

popupCspWaiting.message: CSP: waiting for the site’s header

optSub.message: Turning individual patches on and off. Reload your tabs (F5) after saving.

optResetBtnTitle.message: The same values as a clean install

optResetHint.message: Reset = the values in defaults.js (clientRects off, everything else on).

optRtcHint.message: The WebRTC switch in the popup adds sites to this list. On these sites your real IP is visible — deliberately, so that calls and P2P keep working.

optSwHint.message: The Service Worker switch in the popup adds sites to this list. A site’s own worker reads the REAL machine, and the extension cannot spoof it — only forbid it. Forbidding it turns off offline mode and push notifications on these sites.

optCspClearTitle.message: Restore the site’s own header everywhere

optCspHint.message: The «CSP → workers» switch in the popup adds sites to this list. On these sites Content-Security-Policy is rewritten so that the extension’s workers get through (youtube.com otherwise stands down entirely — see «Limits», item 6). The price: the site’s nonce policy is weakened and its own defence against XSS is lower.

optLearnedH2.message: What the extension learned on its own

optLearnedClearTitle.message: Forget everything learned about site CSP

optLearnedHint.message: Filled in without you: when you open a site the extension remembers what its Content-Security-Policy forbids, so that on the next page it can answer correctly from the first script rather than the second. None of this is visible to the page and none of it leaves the browser, but it is a list of the sites you have visited, and changing profile does not erase it. Clearing is safe: every site will be learned again, at the cost of one page load.

optGeoHint1.message: The extension keeps the browser consistent with itself, but it cannot see which address your requests leave from. A profile can claim Estonia over a German VPN node — and that is visible to any site without a single line of JS. Every 30 minutes cloudflare.com/cdn-cgi/trace is requested, and only the two-letter country code is taken from it; on a mismatch the popup shows a warning under the country name. The country is not switched for you: changing profile mints a new seed and a new visitor id, so that decision is yours.

optGeoHint2.message: This is the only outgoing request the extension makes on its own initiative. Cloudflare learns that there was a request from this address — the same thing it learns when you open almost any site. Neither the profile, nor your history, nor any identifier is sent. Turn it off if you do not need it.

optAuditHint1.message: Checks the extension in the browser it is installed in — not in the one the tests drive. Chrome has refused --load-extension since version 136, so the whole set of suites runs on Chromium, which the extension is never installed into; of the six defects found when moving to Chrome 152, four were invisible to every suite.

optAuditHint2.message: An extension page is not matched by the manifest’s address mask, so content scripts do not run in it and it sees the REAL machine. It asks the service worker for the profile, and reads the page’s values by injecting into the tab you pick. Three sources: what is claimed, what the site sees, what is actually there. Comparing against the claim is the one thing the console checks cannot do: they run inside a patched page themselves, and there is nothing there to compare with.

optWarn1.message: is off by default — otherwise CreepJS often turns red.

optWarn2.message: Stealth mode (popup) switches some patches off by itself; these flags are the base set.

optWarn3.message: «Safe reset» does not change the country, the GPU profile or the seed.

optRtcEmpty.message: The list is empty — WebRTC is protected everywhere.

optRtcCleared.message: WebRTC protection is on for every site. Reload your open tabs.

optSwEmpty.message: The list is empty — service worker is allowed everywhere.

optSwCleared.message: Service Worker is allowed on every site. Reload your open tabs.

optCspEmpty.message: The list is empty — no site headers are rewritten.

optCspCleared.message: Site headers restored everywhere. Reload your open tabs.

optGeoUnknown.message: The exit country is not known yet.

optGeoTurnedOff.message: Country check off, the stored value deleted.

optLearnTte.message: require a TrustedScriptURL at the sink

optLearnNc.message: do not allow blob: in fetch/XHR

optLearnMixed.message: restrict on some routes and not on others

optLearnedCleared.message: Forgotten. Every site will be learned again — at the cost of one page load.

whoTagline.message: What sites see with the current profile

whoParityHint.message: Compares the window, a Worker and an iframe on the key signals in the tab you pick. A divergence is all a site has to see to know it is being lied to.

whoUnscriptable.message: chrome:// pages, the extension web store and tabs that failed to load cannot be scripted — open an ordinary site and refresh the list.

whoPartialScopes.message: Not every scope was checked: the fewer of them answer, the weaker the comparison.

whoVerdictSplits.message: $1 between scopes — a site only has to read one of them twice
